audit.currentFlow: CaseOption mosDocument:<serviceId> overrides mosDocument general list → Case MOS UI needed names → MOS: <name> Task with description.mosDocument {caseId, caseNumber, sentAt}; done/sentAt means submitted. Uploaded CaseDocument files were independent.
persistent: Case MOS fields and cabinet credentials
reusable: in-app Notification / organization automation opt-in / preferences
limitations: MOS requirements and Task state are separate from uploaded files.
No general required/optional readiness or stable per-case snapshot.
Existing DocumentTemplate represents generated DOCX templates, not requirements; it remains unchanged.

schema.flow: Service → ServiceDocumentRequirement → CaseChecklistItem snapshot → existing CaseDocument files; MOS filters those same items by forMos
schema.files: CaseDocument.checklistItemId nullable; one item can link multiple existing files, one file belongs to at most one item; attach requires same Case and scoped access

semantics.snapshots: Atomic on normal Case creation, Lead conversion and CSV import; later template edits never alter existing snapshots.
semantics.existingCases: No automatic backfill. Reads do not write. Explicit initialize maps current service/general requirements and legacy MOS history in one transaction; does not send baseline-ready notifications.
semantics.legacyTemplates: Virtual initial templates preserve service-specific override/general fallback until the admin explicitly saves a service template. Legacy CaseOption records and settings UI remain untouched.
semantics.legacyHistory: Normalize names; retain pending/submitted manual names and notes, skip invalid/cross-tenant references, dedupe by name, preserve latest actual sentAt. Missing sentAt stays null; reminder dueDate is not a submission date. Original Tasks remain intact.
semantics.status: NEEDED → RECEIVED → SUBMITTED_TO_MOS; MOS status is permitted only when forMos. MOS submitted dates preserve literal calendar dates and reject invalid/future dates.
semantics.readiness: All active required items must be RECEIVED or SUBMITTED_TO_MOS. Optional items do not block. Empty/optional-only sets have no blockers, but emit no readiness event.
semantics.merge: Explicit Keep acknowledges the new service without changing items. Merge matches normalized snapshot names, preserves states/files/notes, adds new active requirements, and retains obsolete items with outsideTemplate. Retained required items still block until explicitly archived. Archived items are not silently restored.
semantics.notification: One in-app-only responsible-user notification per real not-ready → ready occurrence; subsequent ready → not-ready → ready creates a new occurrence. Serialized Case mutation and dedupe key commit atomically. No Task or push auto-generation.
semantics.preferences: Uses existing global feature flag and organization opt-in. Honors documents_ready.inApp=false when explicitly stored; no new global push type. Deep link resolves current Case access and opens ?tab=docs; reassignment hides old responsible notifications.
semantics.autosave: Reuses EntityAutosave, minimal item PATCH, item integer CAS, Retry/conflict handling and navigation flush. Collection/template mutations also require CAS. Case autosave updatedAt is independent. Archive, file unlink/deletion and template save remain explicit.
semantics.performance: One shared checklist controller drives desktop/mobile summary, Documents and MOS. Bounded relation fetches; no per-item query in the read payload. Transaction code only uses its supplied transaction client, with Case/service row locks.

compatibility.method: Prisma client generated from origin/main schema performs legacy Case, Service, MOS settings/history and upload reads/writes against the expanded database; no checklist backfill
